children: Many officials at the European Central Bank viewed another rise in the key interest rate as necessary unless there was a significant cooling of the outlook for inflation, according to an account of their deliberations in October released Thursday.
The ECB's governing council last month left its key rate unchanged at 2.5%, having lifted borrowing costs in June and July.
However, investors expect the council to move again next month, a view that will likely be underpinned by the details of their discussions.

"Communication needed to sustain existing policy rate expectations by conveying that another rate hike would likely be necessary unless the inflation outlook improved significantly," members of the council agreed.
In September, the ECB's economists raised their forecast for average inflation in 2027 to 2.5% from 2.3%, further above the 2% target. They will publish new forecasts at next month's meeting.

Developments since the late-October meeting suggest the eurozone's inflation rate may peak at a lower level than then seemed likely, so a December rate rise is by no means certain, although it is likely.
In particular, energy prices have fallen since the outcome of U.S. midterm elections fueled hopes of a resolution to the conflict between the U.S. and Iran.
At the time of the meeting, "a large number" of members of the governing council believed that "a durable resolution of the conflict in the Middle East had become less likely."
Futures prices suggest participants in energy markets do not now agree with that view, and the recent fall in energy prices is likely to have an impact on inflation as soon as this month.

Economists at Barclays estimate that lower fuel prices will lead to a drop in the eurozone's annual rate of inflation to 3.8% in November from 4% in October. They expect the inflation rate to peak at 4.2% in January, and fall gradually to target in the early months of 2028.
